newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - UK's FKI bids for Newman Tonks.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - UK's FKI bids for Newman Tonks.

text.p: Diversified British engineering group FKI Plc was back on the acquisition trail on Tuesday after launching a 195.7 million pounds ($324.7 million) hostile bid for building supplier Newman Tonks Group Plc.

FKI, with four main divisions of material handling, hardware, automotive and engineering, said Newman Tonks' businesses in Britain and Europe would complement its hardware group in North America and create an international hardware business with turnover in excess of 500 million pounds.
"The acquisition of Newman Tonks represents an excellent opportunity to expand FKI's hardware group internationally and in new sectors of the market," said chairman Jeff Whalley.
Newman Tonks did not immediately comment on the bid.

FKI's latest bid brings to an end a busy year on the acquisition front. It recently bought Italian firm Marelli Motori and the Hawker Siddeley Electric power group for a total 235 million, but this is the first hostile bid it has made.
M&G, Newman Tonks' largest shareholder with an 11.18 percent stake in the company, is supporting the offer in common with Britannic Assurance, which has a 2.19 percent holding.
"The M&G and Britannic undertakings are quite significant, they must have become very frustrated with Newman Tonks," Whalley told Reuters in a telephone interview.

FKI's cash and share offer for Newman Tonks equivalent to 150 pence a share values the latter at 195.7 million pounds and represents a 46.3 percent premium to the company's closing share price of 102.5p on December 13. By 1156 GMT, shares in Newman Tonks had risen 19-1/2 pence to stand at 148-1/2.
FKI said that over the last five years, Newman Tonks' financial and share price performance has been dismal.
Shares in Newman Tonks have traded as low as 98 pence this year. FKI said the shares have traded at a 58 percent discount relative to the FT All share index since December 16, 1991.

"1996 has been a year of misery for any holders of Newman Tonks and the stock has gone up in a straight line to the level of the bid," said one equities trader. "I would expect people are just going to say thanks very much'."
There is also a cash alternative to the offer valuing each Newman Tonks share at 140 pence and the company at 182.6 million, representing a 36.6 percent premium to the share price.
The cash alternative will be financed partly from FKI's cash resources and from the proceeds of a conditional rights issue to raise a maximum of 152.4 million pounds.
The rights issue is on the basis of two new FKI shares for every 13 existing shares at 175 pence per share and is conditional upon the offer being declared unconditional.

This would take FKI's gearing to around 80 percent from the post Hawker Siddleley Electric power group purchase level of around 60 percent. FKI said that its interest cover, a measure of a company's ability to pay interest on borrowings, would be strong at around eight times.
